Relocatable paths

paths resolves the five MixOS roots. It has no workspace dependencies. The running binary finds its prefix through /proc/self/exe, following the managed entry link to the real binary, then taking the parent of bin/. Moving that tree requires no rebuild.

RootSystem defaultPrefix under $HOME
prefixDerived from the binaryDerived from the binary
config/etc/mixos$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mixos, else ~/.config/mixos
state/var/lib/mixos$XDG_STATE_HOME/mixos, else ~/.local/state/mixos
cache/var/cache/mixos$XDG_CACHE_HOME/mixos, else ~/.cache/mixos
runtime/run/mixos$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/mixos (required)

Each root takes MIXOS_<ROOT> first, then its key in <prefix>/layout.mx, then the default. The environment prefix also selects where to read layout.mx; a prefix key inside that document does not start another lookup. The document is strict data, with at most five unique keys, each an absolute path string. Unknown keys, relative paths and executable expressions refuse. Empty root overrides refuse rather than falling back.

config: "/srv/example/config"
state: "/srv/example/state"

Rust callers use paths::root(paths::Root::Config), paths::bin("mix"), paths::share("scenes/editor") and paths::resolve("mixos:prefix/share/scenes"). Mix callers use mixos_path("config"), mixos_path("prefix", "bin/mix") or mixos_path("mixos:prefix/share/scenes"). Relative paths cannot escape their root with ... Ordinary user paths are unchanged by resolve.

Saved MixOS paths use mixos:<root>/<relative>. Programs resolve them when opening the file. The old MIXOS, MIXOS_ETC, MIXOS_VAR, MIXOS_RUN, MIXOS_SHARE, MIXOS_BIN and per-app location aliases have no layout role. MIXOS_SRC separately names a development checkout.

Installers select a target independently of their interpreter. The staged binary exposes the defaults from libs/paths without self-location or MIXOS_* overrides:

/path/to/staged/mix layout defaults --tier system --json
/path/to/staged/mix layout defaults --tier user --prefix /home/user/mixos --json

The system installation prefix defaults to /opt/mixos; a user installation requires --prefix. User roots use the caller's XDG environment; an unset runtime is omitted from the JSON and must be supplied explicitly by the installer. Runtime path resolution still derives the prefix from the binary.

tools/gold_release.mix accepts --prefix, --tier, and overrides for the other four roots. It verifies the release before querying its staged Mix. Command-line roots take precedence over the target's existing layout.mx, then the staged binary's defaults. Applying journals the selected layout.mx alongside the installed files. --state selects the state root; release records and backups live beneath its releases/ directory. Rollback/recover can use --receipt-file FILE, or an explicit prefix and target layout (with --state and --receipt ID to locate a saved receipt). They need no running target binary and work under the previous release or mix-static.

tools/component_install.mix uses the same precedence. --root is a staging system root, while --prefix selects the target prefix within that root. --mix STAGED_MIX supplies defaults before a target binary exists; otherwise it queries the target's bin/mix. Complete explicit roots, target layouts or rollback receipts need no defaults query. Component receipts retain the target layout. Neither installer derives the destination from its interpreter.

Repository tools support the previous Mix release. Docs resolve logical paths against the checkout: mixos:prefix/share/x (or mixos:share/x) names <repo>/share/x. Populate pinned font inputs in the ignored share/assets/sets/ with mix share/assets/install.mix --root /absolute/checkout/share/assets before building the site. Dev lint skips installed-asset checks when its interpreter lacks mixos_path.

External files use templates with @{prefix}, @{config}, @{state}, @{cache} and @{runtime} placeholders. Component owners keep their unit templates; packages carry them beneath share/layout/. Apply the layout with:

mix layout apply --dry-run
mix layout apply
mix layout apply --root /tmp/example-root

--root stages writes beneath a throwaway system root. The renderer prints each changed file and is idempotent. It manages the PATH block in .mixrc, the login-shell entry in /etc/shells, and one link to <prefix>/bin/mix: /usr/local/bin/mix on hosts, or /usr/bin/mix with --image. A non-symlink at that link path refuses before writes. It never links mix-static. On hosts with Elixir, the managed link makes mix mean MixOS.

Remote execution selects the mix_bin option, then MIX_REMOTE_BIN, then bare mix on the remote PATH. There is no interpreter-owned mesh host table. Absolute remote binary paths may contain spaces; they are quoted before SSH.

To relocate: stop the affected services, move the prefix, adjust layout.mx for other moved roots, run mix layout apply, then restart. Running processes keep their current paths. The implementation does not migrate live data. tools/layout_migrate_saved.mix previews changes in explicit offline copies, keeps originals when applied, and refuses live-root overlaps. SQLite stores must be exported through their owning component first so audit chains survive.

The path gate runs in tools/lint.mix. The worker release gate also checks default template bytes and runs tests/layout_relocation_test.mix, using a prefix with a space and a private mount namespace. Missing namespace, nested desktop or loopback SSH support is reported explicitly as a skip.

mix tests/layout_templates_test.mix --installed additionally compares the rendered defaults against an existing installed share/units tree and reports any deployment drift, including comments. The normal release check compares against the immutable source baseline.
